turns: My uncle has occupied our ancestral land in the village and got the mutation done in his name. How do I get the land back?

results.reply: Property title disputes, especially involving ancestral land and mutation records, are complex and require a thorough examination of land revenue records and succession documents. This is not a simple matter of a refund or a notice; it involves civil litigation to establish your legal title and challenge the mutation entry. Because this involves your family property rights and potential court proceedings, you should not attempt to handle this alone. I strongly recommend you consult a local civil lawyer who specialises in land revenue matters or contact the free legal aid services for guidance on how to file a suit for partition or declaration of title. You can call the national legal aid helpline at 15100 for assistance in finding a lawyer or understanding your rights under the law.

citations.title: NALSA legal aid helpline 15100
citations.plain: Call the national legal aid helpline 15100 (toll-free) for free legal advice and help applying for legal aid. You can also apply for legal aid or victim compensation online via the NALSA website.
